sections.body:

This module covers:

2. Support Vector Machines (SVM)
3. Decision Trees

Each with:

sections.title: Example 1: Binary Classification (Linearly Separable)
sections.body:
```python
print("Example 1: Binary Classification (Email Spam Detection)")
print("-" * 60)

# Generate synthetic data
np.random.seed(42)
X_linear, y_linear = make_classification(
    n_samples=200, n_features=2, n_redundant=0, n_informative=2,
    n_clusters_per_class=1, flip_y=0.1, random_state=42
)

# Split data
X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(X_linear, y_linear, test_size=0.3, random_state=42)

# Train logistic regression
log_reg = LogisticRegression(random_state=42)
log_reg.fit(X_train, y_train)

# Predictions
y_pred = log_reg.predict(X_test)
y_proba = log_reg.predict_proba(X_test)[:, 1]

# Metrics
accuracy = accuracy_score(y_test, y_pred)
precision = precision_score(y_test, y_pred)
recall = recall_score(y_test, y_pred)
f1 = f1_score(y_test, y_pred)

print(f"Accuracy: {accuracy:.4f}")
print(f"Precision: {precision:.4f} (Of predicted spam, {precision*100:.1f}% actually spam)")
print(f"Recall: {recall:.4f} (Of actual spam, {recall*100:.1f}% detected)")
print(f"F1-Score: {f1:.4f} (Harmonic mean of precision & recall)")
print()

print("Confusion Matrix:")
cm = confusion_matrix(y_test, y_pred)
print(cm)
print(f"  True Negatives: {cm[0,0]} | False Positives: {cm[0,1]}")
print(f"  False Negatives: {cm[1,0]} | True Positives: {cm[1,1]}")
print()

print("Sample Predictions (first 5):")
for i in range(5):
    print(f"  Actual: {y_test[i]}, Predicted: {y_pred[i]}, Probability: {y_proba[i]:.4f}")
print()
```

```python
print("Example 2: Multi-class Classification (Iris Species)")

# Load iris dataset
```

sections.title: Example 3: Probability Calibration
sections.body:
**What this code covers**

- Plot decision boundary for 2D classification
- SECTION 2: SUPPORT VECTOR MACHINES (SVM)…
- Helper function for plotting decision boundaries
- Visualization 1: Logistic Regression
- Plot 1: Decision Boundary
- Plot 2: Sigmoid Function
- Plot 3: ROC Curve
- Plot 4: Confusion Matrix Heatmap

```python
print("Example 3: Understanding Probabilities")
print("-" * 60)

# Generate test samples
np.random.seed(42)
X_new = np.array([[-2, -2], [-1, -1], [0, 0], [1, 1], [2, 2]])

# Get probabilities
probas = log_reg.predict_proba(X_new)
predictions = log_reg.predict(X_new)

print("Sample predictions with probabilities:")
print("-" * 50)
print(f"{'Features':<20} {'P(Class 0)':<15} {'P(Class 1)':<15} {'Prediction':<10}")
print("-" * 50)
for i, (x, prob, pred) in enumerate(zip(X_new, probas, predictions)):
    print(f"{str(x):<20} {prob[0]:<15.4f} {prob[1]:<15.4f} {pred:<10}")
print()
print("✓ Probabilities sum to 1.0 for each sample!")
print("✓ Decision boundary at P = 0.5")
print()

# Helper function for plotting decision boundaries
def plot_decision_boundary(X, y, model, title, ax, resolution=0.02):
    """Plot decision boundary for 2D classification"""
    x_min, x_max = X[:, 0].min() - 1, X[:, 0].max() + 1
    y_min, y_max = X[:, 1].min() - 1, X[:, 1].max() + 1
    
    xx, yy = np.meshgrid(
        np.arange(x_min, x_max, resolution),
        np.arange(y_min, y_max, resolution)
    )
    
    Z = model.predict(np.c_[xx.ravel(), yy.ravel()])
    Z = Z.reshape(xx.shape)
    
    ax.contourf(xx, yy, Z, alpha=0.3, cmap='RdYlBu')
    scatter = ax.scatter(X[:, 0], X[:, 1], c=y, cmap='RdYlBu', 
                        edgecolors='black', s=50, alpha=0.8)
    ax.set_title(title, fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
    ax.set_xlabel('Feature 1', fontsize=12)
    ax.set_ylabel('Feature 2', fontsize=12)
    return scatter

# Visualization 1: Logistic Regression
print("Creating logistic regression visualizations...")
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(15, 12))

# Plot 1: Decision Boundary
ax1 = axes[0, 0]
plot_decision_boundary(X_linear, y_linear, log_reg, 
                      'Logistic Regression Decision Boundary\n(Linear separator)', ax1)

# Plot 2: Sigmoid Function
ax2 = axes[0, 1]
z = np.linspace(-10, 10, 100)
sigmoid = 1 / (1 + np.exp(-z))
ax2.plot(z, sigmoid, linewidth=3, color='blue')
ax2.axhline(y=0.5, color='red', linestyle='--', linewidth=2, alpha=0.7, label='Decision threshold')
ax2.axvline(x=0, color='green', linestyle='--', linewidth=2, alpha=0.7, label='z=0')
ax2.set_xlabel('z (linear combination)', fontsize=12)
ax2.set_ylabel('σ(z) = P(y=1)', fontsize=12)
ax2.set_title('Sigmoid Function\n(Maps any value to [0,1])', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
ax2.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
ax2.legend()

# Plot 3: ROC Curve
ax3 = axes[1, 0]
fpr, tpr, thresholds = roc_curve(y_test, y_proba)
roc_auc = roc_auc_score(y_test, y_proba)

ax3.plot(fpr, tpr, linewidth=3, label=f'ROC curve (AUC = {roc_auc:.3f})', color='blue')
ax3.plot([0, 1], [0, 1], 'r--', linewidth=2, label='Random classifier (AUC = 0.5)')
ax3.set_xlabel('False Positive Rate', fontsize=12)
ax3.set_ylabel('True Positive Rate', fontsize=12)
ax3.set_title('ROC Curve\n(Higher AUC = Better model)', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
ax3.legend()
ax3.grid(True, alpha=0.3)

# Plot 4: Confusion Matrix Heatmap
ax4 = axes[1, 1]
sns.heatmap(cm, annot=True, fmt='d', cmap='Blues', cbar=False, ax=ax4,
            xticklabels=['Not Spam', 'Spam'], yticklabels=['Not Spam', 'Spam'])
ax4.set_xlabel('Predicted Label', fontsize=12)
ax4.set_ylabel('True Label', fontsize=12)
ax4.set_title(f'Confusion Matrix\n(Accuracy = {accuracy:.3f})', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('logistic_regression.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
print("✓ Saved logistic regression visualization")
print()

"""
================================================================================
SECTION 2: SUPPORT VECTOR MACHINES (SVM)
================================================================================

📊 VISUAL INTUITION:
-------------------
SVM finds the "best" line/hyperplane to separate classes:
• Not just any line that separates - the BEST one!
• Best = Maximum margin (widest street between classes)
• Support Vectors = Points closest to boundary (on the street edges)

Think of it like:
- Drawing a road between two neighborhoods
- Make the road as WIDE as possible
- Houses closest to the road define its width

🎯 SIMPLE EXPLANATION:
----------------------
SVM tries to find the separating line with maximum margin:

Margin = Distance from line to nearest point of each class

Key ideas:
1. Maximize the margin (robustness!)
2. Support vectors = Critical points defining the boundary
3. Kernel trick = Handle non-linear boundaries!

For non-linearly separable data:
- RBF Kernel: Creates circular/complex boundaries
- Polynomial Kernel: Creates curved boundaries

🌍 REAL-WORLD USE CASES:
-------------------------
✓ Image Classification: Face recognition, digit recognition
✓ Text Categorization: Topic classification, sentiment analysis
✓ Bioinformatics: Protein classification, gene expression
✓ Handwriting Recognition: Digit/character recognition
✓ Face Detection: Detect faces in images

🔑 KEY CONCEPTS:
----------------
1. **Hyperplane**: Decision boundary (line in 2D, plane in 3D)
   w·x + b = 0

2. **Margin**: Distance to nearest points
   Maximize: 2/||w||

3. **Support Vectors**: Points on the margin
   These are the ONLY points that matter!
   Remove other points → same boundary

4. **Kernels**: Transform data to higher dimensions
   • Linear: K(x,x') = x·x'
   • RBF (Gaussian): K(x,x') = exp(-γ||x-x'||²)
   • Polynomial: K(x,x') = (x·x' + c)^d

5. **C Parameter**: Regularization
   • Small C: Wider margin, more errors (soft margin)
   • Large C: Narrower margin, fewer errors (hard margin)

📐 MATHEMATICAL FOUNDATION:
---------------------------
Primal Problem:
    minimize: (1/2)||w||² + C·Σξᵢ
    subject to: yᵢ(w·xᵢ + b) ≥ 1 - ξᵢ

where ξᵢ = slack variables (allow some errors)

Decision Function:
    f(x) = sign(w·x + b)
    
With kernel:
    f(x) = sign(Σᵢ αᵢyᵢK(xᵢ,x) + b)

Only support vectors have αᵢ > 0!
"""

print("=" * 80)
print("SECTION 2: SUPPORT VECTOR MACHINES (SVM)")
print("=" * 80)
print()
```

sections.title: Example 1: Linear Svm
sections.body:
```python
print("Example 1: Linear SVM (Linearly Separable Data)")
print("-" * 60)

# Generate linearly separable data
np.random.seed(42)
X_svm_linear, y_svm_linear = make_classification(
    n_samples=100, n_features=2, n_redundant=0, n_informative=2,
    n_clusters_per_class=1, flip_y=0.0, class_sep=2.0, random_state=42
)

# Train Linear SVM
svm_linear = SVC(kernel='linear', C=1.0, random_state=42)
svm_linear.fit(X_svm_linear, y_svm_linear)

# Get support vectors
n_support = svm_linear.n_support_
support_vectors = svm_linear.support_vectors_

print(f"Number of support vectors: {sum(n_support)} (out of {len(X_svm_linear)} samples)")
print(f"  Class 0: {n_support[0]} support vectors")
print(f"  Class 1: {n_support[1]} support vectors")
print()

# Score
train_score = svm_linear.score(X_svm_linear, y_svm_linear)
print(f"Training Accuracy: {train_score:.4f}")
print()
```

sections.title: Example 2: Non-linear Svm with Rbf Kernel
sections.body:
```python
print("Example 2: RBF Kernel SVM (Non-linear Boundaries)")
print("-" * 60)

# Generate non-linearly separable data (moons)
X_moons, y_moons = make_moons(n_samples=200, noise=0.15, random_state=42)

# Split data
X_train_moons, X_test_moons, y_train_moons, y_test_moons = train_test_split(
    X_moons, y_moons, test_size=0.3, random_state=42
)

# Standardize features (important for SVM!)
scaler_svm = StandardScaler()
X_train_moons_scaled = scaler_svm.fit_transform(X_train_moons)
X_test_moons_scaled = scaler_svm.transform(X_test_moons)

# Try different kernels
kernels = ['linear', 'rbf', 'poly']
svm_models = {}

for kernel in kernels:
    svm = SVC(kernel=kernel, C=1.0, gamma='scale', random_state=42)
    svm.fit(X_train_moons_scaled, y_train_moons)
    train_acc = svm.score(X_train_moons_scaled, y_train_moons)
    test_acc = svm.score(X_test_moons_scaled, y_test_moons)
    svm_models[kernel] = svm
    
    print(f"{kernel.upper()} Kernel:")
    print(f"  Train Accuracy: {train_acc:.4f}")
    print(f"  Test Accuracy: {test_acc:.4f}")
    print(f"  Support Vectors: {sum(svm.n_support_)}")
    print()

print("✓ RBF kernel handles non-linear boundaries best!")
print()
```

sections.title: Example 3: Effect of C Parameter
sections.body:
**What this code covers**

- SECTION 3: DECISION TREES…
- Generate data with some overlap
- Try different C values
- Plot 1: Linear SVM with Support Vectors
- Plot 2-4: Different Kernels on Moons Data
- Replot linear SVM for moons
- Plot 5-7: Effect of C Parameter

```python
print("Example 3: Effect of C Parameter (Regularization)")
print("-" * 60)

# Generate data with some overlap
X_overlap, y_overlap = make_classification(
    n_samples=100, n_features=2, n_redundant=0, n_informative=2,
    n_clusters_per_class=1, flip_y=0.15, class_sep=1.0, random_state=42
)

# Try different C values
C_values = [0.1, 1.0, 10.0]
svm_c_models = {}

for C in C_values:
    svm = SVC(kernel='linear', C=C, random_state=42)
    svm.fit(X_overlap, y_overlap)
    accuracy = svm.score(X_overlap, y_overlap)
    n_sv = sum(svm.n_support_)
    svm_c_models[C] = svm
    
    print(f"C = {C}:")
    print(f"  Accuracy: {accuracy:.4f}")
    print(f"  Support Vectors: {n_sv}")
    print()

print("✓ Small C: More support vectors, wider margin (more tolerant)")
print("✓ Large C: Fewer support vectors, narrower margin (less tolerant)")
print()

# Visualization 2: SVM
print("Creating SVM visualizations...")
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 3, figsize=(18, 12))

# Plot 1: Linear SVM with Support Vectors
ax1 = axes[0, 0]
plot_decision_boundary(X_svm_linear, y_svm_linear, svm_linear, 
                      'Linear SVM\n(Support Vectors marked)', ax1)
ax1.scatter(support_vectors[:, 0], support_vectors[:, 1], 
           s=200, facecolors='none', edgecolors='red', linewidth=3, 
           label='Support Vectors')
ax1.legend()

# Plot 2-4: Different Kernels on Moons Data
for idx, (kernel, svm) in enumerate(svm_models.items()):
    ax = axes[0, idx] if idx == 0 else axes[0, idx]
    if idx > 0:
        ax = axes[0, idx]
        plot_decision_boundary(X_train_moons_scaled, y_train_moons, svm,
                             f'{kernel.upper()} Kernel\n(Test Acc: {svm.score(X_test_moons_scaled, y_test_moons):.3f})', 
                             ax, resolution=0.05)

# Replot linear SVM for moons
ax = axes[0, 1]
plot_decision_boundary(X_train_moons_scaled, y_train_moons, svm_models['linear'],
                     f'LINEAR Kernel\n(Test Acc: {svm_models["linear"].score(X_test_moons_scaled, y_test_moons):.3f})', 
                     ax, resolution=0.05)

ax = axes[0, 2]
plot_decision_boundary(X_train_moons_scaled, y_train_moons, svm_models['rbf'],
                     f'RBF Kernel\n(Test Acc: {svm_models["rbf"].score(X_test_moons_scaled, y_test_moons):.3f})', 
                     ax, resolution=0.05)

# Plot 5-7: Effect of C Parameter
for idx, (C, svm) in enumerate(svm_c_models.items()):
    ax = axes[1, idx]
    plot_decision_boundary(X_overlap, y_overlap, svm,
                         f'C = {C}\n({sum(svm.n_support_)} Support Vectors)', 
                         ax)
    # Mark support vectors
    sv = svm.support_vectors_
    ax.scatter(sv[:, 0], sv[:, 1], s=150, facecolors='none', 
              edgecolors='red', linewidth=2)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('svm.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
print("✓ Saved SVM visualization")
print()

"""
================================================================================
SECTION 3: DECISION TREES
================================================================================

📊 VISUAL INTUITION:
-------------------
Decision Trees ask a series of YES/NO questions:
• "Is income > $50k?" → YES → "Is age < 30?" → YES → Approve
• Think of "20 Questions" game or medical diagnosis flowchart

Tree structure:
    Root → Branches → Leaves
    
Each split: "What question best separates the classes?"
Uses Information Gain (from Information Theory!)

🎯 SIMPLE EXPLANATION:
----------------------
Decision Tree builds a flowchart of decisions:

1. Start at root (all data)
2. Find best feature to split on (maximize information gain)
3. Split data into branches
4. Repeat for each branch (recursively)
5. Stop when pure (all same class) or max depth reached

Example:
    [All patients]
           ↓
    Is glucose > 140?
       ↙        ↘
    YES          NO
     ↓            ↓
  Diabetes   Is BMI > 30?
             ↙        ↘
           YES        NO
            ↓          ↓
        Diabetes    Healthy

🌍 REAL-WORLD USE CASES:
-------------------------
✓ Medical Diagnosis: Symptom → Disease decision tree
✓ Credit Scoring: Loan approval based on financial features
✓ Customer Segmentation: Demographics → customer type
✓ Fraud Detection: Transaction features → fraud/legitimate
✓ Product Recommendations: User behavior → product suggestions

🔑 KEY CONCEPTS:
----------------
1. **Splitting Criterion**:
   • Classification: Gini Impurity or Entropy (Information Gain)
   • Regression: MSE or MAE

2. **Gini Impurity**: 
   G = 1 - Σpᵢ²
   Measures "impurity" of node
   G = 0: Pure (all same class)
   G = 0.5: Maximum impurity (binary, 50-50 split)

3. **Information Gain** (from Information Theory!):
   IG = H(parent) - Weighted_Average(H(children))
   Choose split with highest IG

4. **Pruning**: Prevent overfitting
   • Pre-pruning: Limit max_depth, min_samples_split
   • Post-pruning: Build full tree, then cut back

5. **Advantages**:
   ✓ Interpretable (visualize tree!)
   ✓ No feature scaling needed
   ✓ Handles non-linear relationships
   ✓ Handles mixed data types
   
6. **Disadvantages**:
   ✗ Prone to overfitting
   ✗ Unstable (small data change → different tree)
   ✗ Biased toward features with many values

📐 MATHEMATICAL FOUNDATION:
---------------------------
Gini Impurity:
    G(node) = 1 - Σᵢ pᵢ²
    where pᵢ = proportion of class i

Entropy:
    H(node) = -Σᵢ pᵢ·log₂(pᵢ)

Information Gain:
    IG(split) = H(parent) - Σⱼ (nⱼ/n)·H(childⱼ)

Splitting:
    For each feature and threshold:
        Calculate IG
    Choose split with maximum IG

Prediction:
    Traverse tree from root to leaf
    Return majority class in leaf
"""

print("=" * 80)
print("SECTION 3: DECISION TREES")
print("=" * 80)
print()
```

sections.title: Example 1: Simple Decision Tree
sections.body:
```python
print("Example 1: Simple Decision Tree (Iris Classification)")
print("-" * 60)

# Load iris dataset (all features this time)
iris = load_iris()
X_tree = iris.data
y_tree = iris.target

# Split data
X_train_tree, X_test_tree, y_train_tree, y_test_tree = train_test_split(
    X_tree, y_tree, test_size=0.3, random_state=42
)

# Train decision tree (limit depth for interpretability)
tree_simple = DecisionTreeClassifier(max_depth=3, random_state=42)
tree_simple.fit(X_train_tree, y_train_tree)

# Evaluate
train_acc_tree = tree_simple.score(X_train_tree, y_train_tree)
test_acc_tree = tree_simple.score(X_test_tree, y_test_tree)

print(f"Train Accuracy: {train_acc_tree:.4f}")
print(f"Test Accuracy: {test_acc_tree:.4f}")
print(f"Tree Depth: {tree_simple.get_depth()}")
print(f"Number of Leaves: {tree_simple.get_n_leaves()}")
print()

# Feature importance
feature_importance = tree_simple.feature_importances_
print("Feature Importance:")
for name, importance in zip(iris.feature_names, feature_importance):
    print(f"  {name:20s}: {importance:.4f}")
print()
```

sections.title: Example 2: Overfitting in Decision Trees
sections.body:
```python
print("Example 2: Overfitting (Effect of max_depth)")
print("-" * 60)

# Try different max depths
depths = [1, 2, 3, 5, 10, None]
train_scores = []
test_scores = []

for depth in depths:
    tree = DecisionTreeClassifier(max_depth=depth, random_state=42)
    tree.fit(X_train_tree, y_train_tree)
    
    train_score = tree.score(X_train_tree, y_train_tree)
    test_score = tree.score(X_test_tree, y_test_tree)
    
    train_scores.append(train_score)
    test_scores.append(test_score)
    
    depth_str = str(depth) if depth is not None else "∞"
    print(f"Max Depth = {depth_str:3s}: Train = {train_score:.4f}, Test = {test_score:.4f}")

print()
optimal_depth = depths[np.argmax(test_scores)]
print(f"✓ Optimal depth: {optimal_depth} (best test accuracy)")
print(f"✓ Unlimited depth often overfits!")
print()
```

sections.title: Example 3: Decision Tree on Non-linear Data
sections.body:
**What this code covers**

- Generate circular data (hard for linear models!)
- Compare with logistic regression
- Visualization 3: Decision Trees
- Plot 1: Tree Structure
- Plot 2: Feature Importance
- Plot 3: Overfitting (Depth vs Accuracy)
- Plot 4: Decision Boundary (Circles - Tree)
- Plot 5: Decision Boundary (Circles - Logistic Regression)

```python
print("Example 3: Decision Tree on Non-linear Data (Circles)")
print("-" * 60)

# Generate circular data (hard for linear models!)
X_circles, y_circles = make_circles(n_samples=300, noise=0.1, factor=0.5, random_state=42)

# Split data
X_train_circ, X_test_circ, y_train_circ, y_test_circ = train_test_split(
    X_circles, y_circles, test_size=0.3, random_state=42
)

# Train decision tree
tree_circles = DecisionTreeClassifier(max_depth=5, random_state=42)
tree_circles.fit(X_train_circ, y_train_circ)

# Compare with logistic regression
log_reg_circles = LogisticRegression(random_state=42)
log_reg_circles.fit(X_train_circ, y_train_circ)

tree_acc = tree_circles.score(X_test_circ, y_test_circ)
log_reg_acc = log_reg_circles.score(X_test_circ, y_test_circ)

print(f"Decision Tree Accuracy: {tree_acc:.4f}")
print(f"Logistic Regression Accuracy: {log_reg_acc:.4f}")
print()
print("✓ Decision Tree handles non-linear boundaries better!")
print("  (Without kernel tricks!)")
print()

# Visualization 3: Decision Trees
print("Creating decision tree visualizations...")
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(18, 12))

# Plot 1: Tree Structure
ax1 = plt.subplot(2, 3, (1, 4))
plot_tree(tree_simple, feature_names=iris.feature_names, class_names=iris.target_names,
         filled=True, rounded=True, fontsize=9, ax=ax1)
ax1.set_title('Decision Tree Structure\n(Iris Classification, max_depth=3)', 
             fontsize=14, fontweight='bold', pad=20)

# Plot 2: Feature Importance
ax2 = plt.subplot(2, 3, 2)
colors = ['green' if imp > 0.1 else 'gray' for imp in feature_importance]
bars = ax2.barh(iris.feature_names, feature_importance, color=colors, alpha=0.7)
ax2.set_xlabel('Importance', fontsize=12)
ax2.set_title('Feature Importance\n(Higher = More important)', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
ax2.grid(True, alpha=0.3, axis='x')

# Plot 3: Overfitting (Depth vs Accuracy)
ax3 = plt.subplot(2, 3, 3)
depths_plot = [d if d is not None else 15 for d in depths]
ax3.plot(depths_plot, train_scores, 'o-', linewidth=2, label='Train Accuracy', markersize=8)
ax3.plot(depths_plot, test_scores, 's-', linewidth=2, label='Test Accuracy', markersize=8)
ax3.axvline(x=optimal_depth, color='green', linestyle='--', linewidth=2, 
           label=f'Optimal depth={optimal_depth}')
ax3.set_xlabel('Max Depth', fontsize=12)
ax3.set_ylabel('Accuracy', fontsize=12)
ax3.set_title('Overfitting: Depth vs Accuracy\n(Gap indicates overfitting)', 
             fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
ax3.legend()
ax3.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
ax3.set_xticks(depths_plot)
ax3.set_xticklabels([str(d) if d is not None else '∞' for d in depths])

# Plot 4: Decision Boundary (Circles - Tree)
ax4 = plt.subplot(2, 3, 5)
plot_decision_boundary(X_circles, y_circles, tree_circles,
                      f'Decision Tree (Circles)\nAccuracy: {tree_acc:.3f}', ax4)

# Plot 5: Decision Boundary (Circles - Logistic Regression)
ax5 = plt.subplot(2, 3, 6)
plot_decision_boundary(X_circles, y_circles, log_reg_circles,
                      f'Logistic Regression (Circles)\nAccuracy: {log_reg_acc:.3f}', ax5)
```
